abstract: This document is a brief glossary of basic statistics vocabulary. It defines three measures of central tendency, namely the mean as the arithmetic average, the median as the middle value when ordered, and the mode as the most frequent value. It also covers two measures of spread, variance as the average of squared deviations from the mean and standard deviation as the square root of the variance. It closes with the p-value, described as the probability of a result at least as extreme under the null hypothesis.
headline: A short glossary defining six core statistics terms: mean, median, mode, variance, standard deviation, and p-value.
key_points: The mean is the arithmetic average of a set of numbers.
The median is the middle value when the numbers are ordered.
The mode is the most frequently occurring value in a set.
Variance is the average of the squared deviations from the mean.
Standard deviation is the square root of the variance.
A p-value is the probability of a result at least as extreme as the observed one, assuming the null hypothesis is true.
